name: Balkans
notes: Mild spring weather, ahead of the summer crowds and heat — fits a deliberately early start to the whole expedition.

name: Turkey
notes: Following on from the Balkans, still ahead of the worst summer heat in Cappadocia and the interior.

name: Caucasus
notes: Mountain passes and Svaneti are snow-free then; connects directly with the Central Asian mountain season.

name: Central Asia
notes: The Pamir Highway and high-altitude passes are only passable in these months — outside this window there is snow/ice. Turkmenistan has been deliberately cut (hard to visit / not realistic for this travel style), and Nur-Sultan/Astana has been dropped (it lay too far out of the route).

name: China
notes: After the summer crowds/heat, well ahead of the Mongolian winter cold that follows. Xinjiang has been deliberately cut (socio-political reasons); Zhangjiajie and Guilin/Yangshuo replace it.

name: Mongolia
notes: Before the freezing cold sets in from October; the Gobi is still dry and warm enough then for a multi-day 4x4 trip.

name: Japan
notes: Autumn colours, and quieter than the cherry-blossom crowds in spring.

name: Taiwan
notes: Dry and mild, ahead of the cooler winter season in the north of the island.

name: Mainland Southeast Asia
notes: The dry season on mainland Southeast Asia — no monsoon, pleasant temperatures. Myanmar has been deliberately cut (hard to visit / not realistic for this travel style). Order reversed (2026-08): Vietnam → Cambodia → Laos → Thailand, via the classic Mekong Delta and Huay Xai border crossings, instead of the earlier Vietnam-Laos order which required an unnecessary backtrack to the north.

name: Maritime Southeast Asia
notes: Still dry in most regions, ahead of the monsoon that starts later in spring. Malaysia has been expanded (2026-08) with a Borneo leg (Sarawak → Brunei → Sabah, the well-known "Borneo Overland Trail") between the peninsula and Brunei — as a result, Malaysia appears twice in this route.

name: Indonesia & East Timor
notes: Dry season continues in most regions until April/May. Java and Bali have been deliberately cut (already visited) — Sumatra replaces them. East Timor connects logically here, via the land border at Kupang (West Timor).

name: Singapore Finale
notes: A deliberate, compact finale to the whole Eurasia expedition — a quiet city stop after East Timor.

name: Mexico
notes: Dry season, after the summer rains.

name: Northern Central America
notes: Dry season, hurricane season over.

name: Southern Central America
notes: Pacific dry season in Costa Rica/Panama — best time for the coast.

name: Colombia
notes: Dry in both the Caribbean region and the coffee zone/Andes.

name: Ecuador
notes: Sierra dry enough for hiking; Galápagos is good year-round but quieter in this season.

name: Peru
notes: The Andes dry season begins — ideal for Cusco/Sacred Valley and Huaraz trekking.

name: Bolivia
notes: Dry season, clear Uyuni Salt Flat (note: no mirror effect like in the wet season — a deliberate trade-off).

name: Northern Chile
notes: Northern Chile only (Atacama, Antofagasta) — Patagonia is a separate future expedition. The Atacama is dry year-round; cold nights in the Chilean winter, fine during the day.

name: Northern Argentina
notes: Northern Argentina only (Salta, Jujuy) — Patagonia is a separate future expedition. Dry peak season in Salta/Jujuy, cold nights in the high mountains.

name: Southern Brazil
notes: Southern Brazil only — Northern Brazil is a separate future expedition. Southern Brazilian winter: mild and dry for sightseeing (Iguaçu, colonial towns), but not beach weather; for beach time start the whole trip 1-2 months later.

name: South Africa, Lesotho & Eswatini
notes: The opener of the expedition, with a real international airport as the entry point (Cape Town/Johannesburg) — Kruger wildlife spotting is at its best here, well before the rainy season.

name: Southern Africa
notes: From Mozambique to Malawi via Zimbabwe, Botswana, Namibia, Angola and Zambia — with this order it falls almost entirely within the dry season (May-October), with the best wildlife viewing right toward the end (August-October). The Angola-Zambia border crossing in southeastern Angola is less traveled than the rest of this route — check extra carefully beforehand.

name: Islands
notes: Madagascar and Mauritius — Madagascar's notoriously slow roads are the biggest time sink here, not the sights themselves.

name: East Africa
notes: Tanzania, Rwanda, Uganda and Kenya — lands in the short rains (October-December, light afternoon showers, manageable) and the following short dry spell (January-February), including the southern Serengeti's calving season. Not the absolute peak (June-October, which here coincides with Southern Africa's only good season), but a recognized strong alternative.

name: Horn of Africa & Egypt
notes: Ethiopia and Egypt as the finale. Ethiopia's main rainy season (kiremt) falls June-September — the old order accidentally dropped Ethiopia right in the middle of it; here it lands in its own good window (October-March, peak December-February). As an added bonus, Egypt benefits from the cooler late season instead of the early summer heat.

name: Iberia & Maghreb
notes: From Moorish Spain via Berber culture in Morocco to Punic/Roman Tunisia — the western Mediterranean where Phoenicians, Carthaginians, Romans and the Islamic world succeeded one another.

name: Malta & Italy
notes: From temples older than the pyramids (Malta) via Magna Graecia and Roman southern Italy to the heart of the Roman Empire, with Sardinia's Nuraghe civilization as a unique finale.

name: Corsica & Southern France
notes: Two French legs connecting Bonifacio's cliffs and the Gallo-Roman monuments of Provence, before the trip crosses the Aegean Sea by flight.

name: Greece & Cyprus
notes: From Greek antiquity on the mainland via the Minoan civilization of Crete to the Greek-Roman-Byzantine layer of Cyprus, just before the crossing to Anatolia.

name: Anatolia
notes: One big leg bringing together Byzantium, the Ottoman Empire and the Roman cities of the Aegean coast, with Cappadocia as a bridge to the rest of Anatolia.

name: Egypt & the Arabian Peninsula
notes: From ancient Egyptian civilization via the Nabataean trade routes of Jordan and the Arab trading world of Oman and the Dilmun civilization of Bahrain to modern Qatar as a deliberately contemporary finale.

name: Scandinavia
notes: Lapland and Norwegian fjords/islands by train and bus — the only leg of this expedition still doable overland.

name: North Atlantic Islands
notes: Svalbard, Denmark, the Faroe Islands, Iceland and Greenland — each one a separate flight hop, not a continuous route; budget in weather buffers.

name: Atlantic Canada – Nova Scotia
notes: Starting point of the expedition — flight Netherlands-Halifax. Rugged coast, fishing villages and lighthouses; no rental car needed, everything is doable via short distances from Halifax.

name: Eastern Canada – Historic Cities
notes: Traveling by train, no rental car in this block. Niagara Falls is an optional day trip from Toronto, not a separate block.

name: Canadian Rockies
notes: Rental car 2 (Calgary-Vancouver). Plan for at least 2-3 nights per national park so you can also hike, not just drive through.

name: Vancouver
notes: No rental car needed in Vancouver itself. Research train vs. bus vs. short flight to Seattle — train is the most scenic and simplest regarding the border.

name: Pacific Northwest & Northern California Roadtrip
notes: Rental car 3 (Seattle-San Francisco). Relaxed pace: better to spend 2-3 nights at a park than drive every day — this is a coastal route, not a race.

name: California Finale
notes: Book Yosemite Valley accommodation well in advance (limited spots permitted during high season). Watch for wildfire risk/air quality in August — check current park alerts shortly before departure.

name: Pacific Opener
notes: Five island groups in the dry season, well before cyclone season (November-April) — the calm, relaxed opener of the expedition.

name: Tropical Australia
notes: Dry season: the Kimberley roads are passable, no monsoon, no jellyfish season near Cairns.

name: Temperate Australia
notes: Late winter/early spring — cooler than the summer peak (December-February), but manageable; the deliberate compromise of this route (see the whole expedition's climate reasoning).

name: New Zealand Finale
notes: Spring — stable weather, quieter than the summer rush (December-February); often recommended by travel guides as a shoulder season. The emotional highlight of the whole expedition, deliberately chosen as the closer.

name: Greater Antilles
notes: Dry season, well after hurricane season (which runs June-November) — a safe, pleasant opener.

name: Dutch Caribbean
notes: Dry season — clearer water for snorkeling and diving.

name: Lesser Antilles
notes: Dry season (carême) — the best time to hike Dominica's rainforest. The island order follows the natural north-south chain, and coincidentally also the L'Express des Îles ferry line.

name: Suriname & Amazon
notes: Suriname's short dry spell lines up perfectly here for jungle/river trips. Northern Brazil's dune coast (Jericoacoara/Lençóis) is then just outside its absolute peak season (June-January) — the only accepted compromise of the whole route.

name: Cape Verde Islands
notes: Just after the rainy season (August-October) — the dry season lasts until June. A calm, pleasant opener.

name: Senegambia
notes: Start of the West African dry season (November-April).

name: Gulf of Guinea
notes: Harmattan season — dry but dusty, the best period to travel here.

name: Central Africa & Islands
notes: Cameroon's least wet period (November-February) and Gabon's short dry season (December-February) coincide here; São Tomé is the exception (rainy season, see the climate reasoning for the whole route).

name: Alpine Countries
notes: Mountain passes and high-altitude hiking trails are only fully snow-free from mid-May/June onward (the Grossglockner High Alpine Road usually opens mid-May) — mid-June to early July is the best window, right after the opening and still ahead of the July crowds/heat in the valleys.

name: Dolomites & Northern Italy
notes: The Dolomites right after the Alpine Countries opener; Milan/Turin/Cinque Terre/Tuscany/San Marino together form one continuous loop instead of two separate southward detours (see the route notes).

name: Balkans
notes: May-June and September are nicest here, and July-August can be warm but is manageable — the waterfalls at Plitvice still have plenty of water then.

name: Central Europe
notes: The High Tatras stay well within the hiking season (June-September); the return route through Czechia/Poland/Germany is pleasant year-round and offers nice autumn colors in September.

name: England & Wales
notes: The opening of the expedition: from the chalk cliffs and historic towns of Southern England via rugged Cornwall to the mountains of Wales, with Isle of Man as a side trip from the Lake District (route-logic fix 2026-08, see the legs below) before the route turns north via Yorkshire/Northumberland towards Scotland.

name: Scotland & Northern Ireland
notes: The single largest component of the whole expedition — the Scottish Highlands and islands, followed by the Northern Irish coast — and the window where the start-in-June plan matters most: well ahead of the midge peak in July-August.

name: Ireland
notes: From Donegal in the northwest via the west coast to Kerry, then southeast to Rosslare — deliberately driven north-to-south so that after the south coast the route can exit directly via Rosslare, without having to go back to Dublin.

name: Channel Islands & Brittany
notes: From the British Crown Dependencies in the Channel (with their own occupation history from the Second World War) to the Celtic culture and megaliths of Brittany — the best autumn window before French coastal weather turns in November.

name: Normandy, Opal Coast & Belgium
notes: The final French legs and Belgium as a quiet finale, just inside the last good autumn window before the coast turns wet and dark in November.
